nodes.description: Root cause. The non-top-level EOF branch falls through to plain `delete element` instead of the parser's destructor-only `delete_Element(element)` cleanup for `StackAllocator`-backed `Element` objects.
ASan sink. Plain `delete` passes a parser `StackAllocator` suballocation to `operator delete(void*)`.

nodes.state: The tracked `element` is constructed by `new_Element(*n, parser)`, i.e. placement new on parser `StackAllocator` storage rather than ordinary heap `new` storage.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `stack_element_alloc.allocator_owns_element == 1` at the tracked allocation event.
operands: the ownership fact corresponding to `new_Element(*n, parser)`; `new_Element` expands to placement new on `allocator.Allocate(sizeof(Element))`, so the constructed `element` is parser `StackAllocator` storage rather than ordinary `new` storage
